what: The entries where Vector 2.0 is known or suspected to differ from the base table. Everything else is inherited. The base table's manual and firmware values come from Anki-era sources (TRM 2021.02.14, the victor firmware), which predate 2.0. Its measured and fitted values come from the household's unit 1, a Vector 1.0; they are marked 'inherited' when this set is loaded. The household's 2.0 is unit 3; its camera overrides now use the calibration it reports.
identify: The robot's factory record (EMR, /dev/mmcblk0p29) holds HW_VER at offset 4 (TRM table 10); DDL's boot display code treats hw_ver >= 0x20 as 2.0 (VICOSLCD). On the body, 1.0 prints an 8-character 'S/N' near the top of the track, 2.0 an 'ESN' on the bottom (ANKISUP). The SDK reports no hardware revision.
inherited_note: measured or fitted on unit 1, a Vector 1.0; not verified on a Vector 2.0

R247.what: Robotics 24/7, 'Digital Dream Labs ships upgraded Vector 2.0 social robot': a 2-megapixel camera, new battery capacity, up to 30 % longer runtime

WEVOLVER.what: Wevolver spec page for Vector 2.0, a spec aggregator: '120 degree field of view'. One source, not confirmed elsewhere.

ANKISUP.what: Anki/DDL support article 338, where to find Vector's serial number on 1.0 and 2.0

REC_Unit3_SWEEP.what: Unit 3 (unit 0a1b2c3d, the household's Vector 2.0) standing still off the dock on the shelf, lift down, head swept over 0, 25, -15, 40, 10 and 0 degrees with the chassis uncommanded, at two spots (B, A) and headings 0 and 180, each reached from both turn directions, plus heading 90 at A. SDK samples taken by a lane on 2026-11-20; the decomposition and the fit-on-B, score-on-A protocol are the another substrate's (the lab's coordination room turn 166). Copied from that lane's publish tree, commit 94a78b1, evidence/head-sweep. Heading is the robot's odometry. Unit 3's printed lift and missing faceplate do not touch the IMU in the head.
REC_Unit3_SWEEP.where: evidence/head-sweep-unit3-20261120/samples.csv (1,494 rows; 24 settled windows at B, 24 at A at headings 0 and 180, 6 at A at 90 after the gates of simulacrum/imu_fit.py) and marks.csv

cube_accel_word_format.source: REC: evidence/unit3-cube-accelerometer/resting.tsv. The observed signed word lattice is 4k+1 on all axes, including both held-out captures.
cube_accel_word_format.note: Empirical packet format for this particular cube. It does not establish the chip identity or its effective analog resolution.

cube_accel_scale.source: REC: evidence/unit3-cube-accelerometer/resting.csv. Effective gain from 1929 upright samples, transferred to the sideways cube in evidence/unit3-wheelstand/R8/settled.csv.gz and the independent R9 pre-command capture.
cube_accel_scale.note: Shelf cube only. The shared Y/Z gain describes the two observed positive-gravity faces. X retains nominal gain. Opposite faces are needed to separate bias from gain. Bounds retain the original sensitivity range.

cube_accel_noise_density_ug.source: REC: evidence/unit3-cube-accelerometer/resting.tsv. Unit 3 shelf cube. Within-packet successive sample differences, 643 stationary packets. Independent undock-check and pre-pickup recordings both improve versus the datasheet nominal. See evidence/unit3-cube-accelerometer/stationary-noise.csv.
cube_accel_noise_density_ug.note: Bounds are a sensitivity range, not a confidence interval. Effective white-noise density for the current filter and quantization model. Specific to the recorded cube; a replacement cube requires its own check.

display_resolution_px.source: VICOSLCD: the MIDAS panel used when hw_ver >= 0x20; VDOCS agrees

battery_capacity_mah.source: No source states the 2.0 capacity. R247 quotes DDL: a new battery and up to 30 % longer runtime; 320 mAh (TRM 6.1.1) x 1.3 is 416, at the same draw. One AI-directory listing gives 600 mAh, unconfirmed; it is the high bound.
battery_capacity_mah.note: Not used by the dynamics; the voltage is (battery_rest_voltage_v).

total_mass_g.source: No source gives the 2.0 mass. The base table's value, with the range widened upward by the author for the new battery and its removable compartment (R247, VDOCS).

com_x_mm.source: No source states it for 2.0. The base table's value and range, widened by 3 mm each way by the author because the battery and its compartment changed (R247, VDOCS) and the battery is the heaviest part whose place is not known. The rear wheelstand measures it (README).

com_z_mm.source: No source states it for 2.0. The base table's value and range, widened by 3 mm each way by the author for the same reason as com_x_mm. The side wheelstand measures it.

camera_fov_horizontal_deg.source: P2CAM: reported fov_x on one Vector 2.0.

camera_fov_vertical_deg.source: P2CAM: reported fov_y on one Vector 2.0.

camera_resolution_px.source: P2CAM: decoded CameraFeed JPEG dimensions on one Vector 2.0.

accel_scale.source: x 1.0140 (1.0085 to 1.0207). Fitted by simulacrum/imu_fit.py head_sweep() on REC_Unit3_SWEEP: tilt, pitch, three offsets and the x scale over spot B's 24 windows, gravity 9806.65 mm/s^2. Held out, spot A: vector error 7.51 mg with the x scale fixed at 1, 6.49 mg with it fitted (24 windows); 5.82 to 3.95 mg at heading 90 (6 windows); 6.71 to 5.31 mg on B itself. A 200-draw bootstrap over B's windows gives the bracketed 95 percent ranges. The another substrate's own fit, at gravity 9810, gave x scale 1.0138 (1.0094 to 1.0190) and offsets 13.2, 3.9, -18.5 mg. y and z stay at 1 and take the part's range (BMI160DS:390-393): from -15 to 40 degrees of head the z axis's share of gravity changes by about a quarter, too little to tell its scale from its offset, and no recording rolls the robot onto its side to show y's.
accel_scale.note: A head-angle scale error (the encoder reading 1.4 % more or less than the true angle) would shift x in nearly the same way; this fit did not test that alternative. It also leaves the ~15 mg opposite-heading difference unexplained.

accel_bias_mg.source: 13.2 (9.5 to 16.4), 4.0 (3.3 to 4.8), -18.1 (-18.6 to -17.8) mg, fitted with the x scale. With the scale fixed at 1 the x offset is 18.1 mg. Fitted by simulacrum/imu_fit.py head_sweep() on REC_Unit3_SWEEP: tilt, pitch, three offsets and the x scale over spot B's 24 windows, gravity 9806.65 mm/s^2. Held out, spot A: vector error 7.51 mg with the x scale fixed at 1, 6.49 mg with it fitted (24 windows); 5.82 to 3.95 mg at heading 90 (6 windows); 6.71 to 5.31 mg on B itself. A 200-draw bootstrap over B's windows gives the bracketed 95 percent ranges. The another substrate's own fit, at gravity 9810, gave x scale 1.0138 (1.0094 to 1.0190) and offsets 13.2, 3.9, -18.5 mg. The range of +/-10 mg is the author's allowance for temperature and for what the fit cannot see, as in the base table.
accel_bias_mg.note: A fact about unit 3. Widen to +/-40 mg per axis to train for any 2.0.

imu_pitch_offset_deg.source: -0.05 (-0.22 to 0.12) deg, fitted with the x scale; -0.22 with it fixed at 1. Fitted by simulacrum/imu_fit.py head_sweep() on REC_Unit3_SWEEP: tilt, pitch, three offsets and the x scale over spot B's 24 windows, gravity 9806.65 mm/s^2. Held out, spot A: vector error 7.51 mg with the x scale fixed at 1, 6.49 mg with it fitted (24 windows); 5.82 to 3.95 mg at heading 90 (6 windows); 6.71 to 5.31 mg on B itself. A 200-draw bootstrap over B's windows gives the bracketed 95 percent ranges. The another substrate's own fit, at gravity 9810, gave x scale 1.0138 (1.0094 to 1.0190) and offsets 13.2, 3.9, -18.5 mg. The range of +/-0.5 deg is the author's allowance, matching the base table's width.
imu_pitch_offset_deg.note: As in the base table: stance on the treads, mounting and the head angle's zero, not separated.
